question: As an expert witness in court, a doctor may express opinions on matters beyond direct personal observation, unlike an ordinary witness who is restricted to facts they personally perceived.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. An expert witness (governed by BSA 2023, Section 45) is permitted to give opinion evidence based on specialised knowledge. This is the entire purpose of calling a forensic expert — the court lacks that expertise itself.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. This is the defining distinction of an expert witness under Section 45 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) 2023. An ordinary witness can only testify to what they directly perceived; an expert witness is specifically called to give an opinion based on specialised knowledge, training, and experience.
